questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent dangerous problems. Small issues on a motorcycle can cause more serious problems than on a car.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Encourage them to take less-crowded roads.
Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
The effects are less dangerous than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including some over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. These drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use your turn signals when you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: What is true about intersections for riders?

options.text: They are safe because of heavy traffic.
They are dangerous spots for riders.
They are safer than open roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are dangerous spots for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because that is where motorcyclists and other drivers are most likely to have conflicts.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks, loose padding, or damage.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no damage like cracks or loose padding. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: You do not need to look over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will respond correctly to your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do about riding?

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a limit beforehand so you can still ride safely.
Do not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even small amounts can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: For best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: For best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials work best.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have which types of brakes?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Sudden moves could cause the motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to escape a slippery road.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Using signals properly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a dangerously slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen by:

options.text: Letting the front tire lock up.
Using both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually to stop shortest and safest. Do not lock up either tire.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look 12 seconds ahead and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: The accelerator is controlled with:
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with the right hand.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is that:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is unsafe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you better.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down a motorcycle. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, check all of the following except:

options.text: Both brakes activate the brake light.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and all lights including the headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash. It also shields you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up from other vehicles.
